title: Matched-initial-state fixed-flow versus fully coupled comparison
scientific_question: How much does time-dependent hydrodynamic feedback change the thermal step response when both calculations start from exactly the same three-dimensional state?
fixed_flow_reference: The existing P418 fixed-flow step cases use target-endpoint U, p, p_rgh and phi together with source-endpoint fluid and solid temperature fields.
fully_coupled_candidate: Use byte-identical time-zero fields and target boundary conditions, but enable continuity and momentum together with the two energy equations after t=0.
reason: The previous source-flow initialization mixed hydrodynamic feedback with a large inlet/interior flow mismatch, especially for the 0.05 to 0.25 m/s velocity step.
representative_sequence_reason: The source step changes heat generation while inlet velocity is unchanged, providing the cleanest first check of flow-thermal feedback.
required_pre_solver_checks: all six time-zero fields are byte-identical between fixed-flow and fully coupled cases
fluid and solid transient schemes use Euler
flow and momentumPredictor are enabled only in the fully coupled candidate
mesh, material properties, boundary values and heat source remain unchanged
the OpenFOAM solver is not called during preparation
